meaning: The number 52 is best known as the number of days Nehemiah took to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem, symbolizing the completion of a divine mission through perseverance and faith.
description: In Nehemiah 6:15 it is told that the walls around Jerusalem were rebuilt in 52 days, despite strong resistance from enemies. This was seen as a powerful sign of God's faithfulness and protection of His people—an apparently impossible task completed in a short time because God Himself stood behind the work. The number 52 can thus be understood as a symbol that divine missions are accomplished when people act in obedience and faith, regardless of external opposition.

versions.meaning: The number 52 is best known as the number of weeks Nehemiah took to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem, symbolizing the completion of a divine mission through perseverance and faith.
versions.description: In Nehemiah 6:15 it is told that the walls around Jerusalem were rebuilt in 52 days, which is interpreted as a symbol of God's faithfulness and protection of His people. The number has also been linked to completeness in Jewish tradition, partly because the Jewish year has about 52 weeks. Some rabbinic interpretations see the number as a reminder of cyclical renewal and divine order in time. However, it is not among the most central symbolic numbers in biblical numerology, such as 7, 12 or 40.

footnotes.text: The Jewish year has approximately 52 weeks, and some rabbinic interpretations therefore link the number 52 to cyclical renewal and divine order in time.

52 is not among the most central symbolic numbers in biblical numerology (such as 7, 12, or 40), but the story of Nehemiah gives it a clear theological meaning connected to restoration and completion.
The Jewish historian Josephus confirms the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls under Nehemiah, and archaeological findings support the existence of the city gate and wall structures from this period.
